scope: Two additional primary experiments introduced by the user-requested cross-species follow-up. These are additions after quantitative_references.json was delivered.

references.authors: Dong VNK, Tantisuwat L, Setthawong P, Tharasanit T, Sutayatram S, Kijtawornrat A
references.title: The Preliminary Chronic Effects of Electromagnetic Radiation from Mobile Phones on Heart Rate Variability, Cardiac Function, Blood Profiles, and Semen Quality in Healthy Dogs
references.finding: Seven analysed male beagles showed no significant change in measured semen endpoints after a 10-week mobile-phone protocol at 1962–1966 MHz, 120 one-minute ringing periods/day, five days/week, with two phones on the chest. The quoted 0.96 W/kg was manufacturer phone SAR, not canine testis dosimetry; comparison was to baseline without a concurrent sham group.
references.verification: Full primary XML checked via Europe PMC. Eight recruited, one excluded at baseline for ventricular ectopy, seven analysed. Semen at baseline/weeks 5/10. Mean motility 83.0/80.0/85.0%; no significant differences in semen volume, sperm concentration, morphology, motility, viability or DNA integrity.

references.authors: Berlinguer F, Pasciu V, Succu S, Cossu I, Caggiu S, Addis D, Castagna A, Fontani V, Rinaldi S, Sanna Passino E
references.title: REAC technology as optimizer of stallion spermatozoa liquid storage
references.finding: In paired aliquots from sixteen ejaculates of eight stallions, a 2.4 GHz REAC device with contact electrodes immersed in semen medium preserved DNA and acrosome integrity and antioxidant measures during 72-hour storage at 4 °C. Progressive motility and viability did not improve. The result concerns the combined device intervention, not an isolated environmental RF exposure.
references.verification: Publisher full text and Europe PMC XML checked. Treated/control samples were held in separate refrigerators. Numerical tissue/sample SAR and a dose gradient were not supplied. Two authors declared that they invented the REAC technology. Several p-value inequality typos occur in abstract/figure captions; finding uses the result direction and body text, not those typos.
